content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Bitcoin payment

Bitcoin payments for digital downloads are not a workaround but a foundation for sovereignty in commerce. In regions where payment gateways fail, creators lose revenue to platform fees or outright block lists. COREMERCH replaces that with a stack built entirely on free or low‑cost public infrastructure: GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and NOWPayments for instant on‑chain confirmation. The stack removes the 10% cut that Gumroad applies and reduces it to 0.5%, meaning that at 100 sales on a $97 product you keep an extra $921 per month. This financial advantage translates directly into higher profit margins and the ability to reinvest in product creation instead of paying fees. The stack’s architecture is also resilient to currency collapse and regulatory clamp‑downs because it never relies on a single financial institution.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

At the core of the stack is a static site hosted on a global CDN, ensuring minimal latency for buyers worldwide. When a buyer clicks “Buy”, a short‑lived token is issued by Cloudflare Workers or Apps Script which embeds the product ID and payment amount. That token is sent to NOWPayments, which monitors the chosen blockchain network—BSC, Solana, or TRON—for a valid transaction that matches the USD equivalent at the moment of payment. As soon as the blockchain confirms the transaction, NOWPayments triggers a webhook that the worker receives. The worker then streams the digital asset directly from Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to the buyer, eliminating the need for a separate download server. The entire flow is stateless, auditable, and free of proprietary dependencies.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The stack is engineered for creators who produce ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, and software—any product that can be delivered digitally. It is ideal for those in countries where traditional gateways are blocked or unreliable, such as Venezuela, Zimbabwe, and the Philippines. By owning the code and infrastructure, creators avoid platform lock‑in and can respond instantly to regulatory changes. The stack also caters to seasoned developers who value a clean, modular architecture that can be integrated into existing workflows, while still being accessible to those with limited technical experience. Ultimately, it is a tool for creators who demand full control over their sales funnel and data, without paying a premium to third‑party platforms.
Automated delivery means the download link arrives before the buyer navigates away from the payment confirmation page.
The Components That Make It Work Together

GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages provide the static front‑end, delivering a lightning‑fast storefront. Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script act as the serverless backend, handling payment token generation, webhook processing, and delivery logic. NOWPayments is the payment processor, offering 300+ cryptocurrencies and instant on‑chain verification with zero KYC. Supabase or Google Sheets store order metadata, allowing creators to track sales and analytics. Finally, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 stores the product files, ensuring scalable, secure, and cost‑effective delivery. Together, these components form a coherent, low‑budget stack that eliminates the need for any subscription or platform fee.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

Scaling a sovereign digital store requires no infrastructure changes at any realistic volume level for most individual creators. Cloudflare Workers processes each webhook event independently — ten simultaneous orders are handled as ten separate processes with no queue congestion. Supabase handles hundreds of concurrent database operations on the free tier. Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month on the free tier — enough for significant daily sales volume. Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront to any number of concurrent visitors without capacity constraints. NOWPayments processes payment volume without per-transaction approval delays.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

Selling digital products without PayPal or Stripe is not a compromise — it is an upgrade for creators in restricted markets. The conventional platforms that seem like the standard path come with payout delays, geographic restrictions, platform fees of 5 to 10 percent, and the permanent risk of account suspension. A sovereign stack has none of these constraints. Your product page loads on Cloudflare Pages. Your buyer pays in USDT or Bitcoin through a NOWPayments checkout with live price feeds and QR code generation. Your backend verifies the payment on-chain and sends the download link within 30 seconds.
Every digital file type — ebooks, fonts, presets, plugins, templates — works with the same automated delivery pipeline.

Every digital product type — ebook, course, template, font, preset, beat, plugin, software license — works with the same sovereign commerce infrastructure. You build the product. NOWPayments handles the checkout. Your backend handles the delivery. You keep 99.5% of every sale. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy the complete stack under your accounts in 48 hours. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything you need to build it yourself. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. See both at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Build your product before you build your store — the product is the point, not the infrastructure. Once your product is ready and in delivery-ready format, create your NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses. Choose Stack 01 for self-deployment following the Blueprint, or Stack 02 for COREMERCH deployment. Upload your product file to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and note the file path. Configure the product in your backend with the file path, USD price, and delivery email template. Build your product page on the storefront with clear product description, pricing in USD, and the checkout flow. Run a complete mainnet test. Check that the download link works and expires correctly after the configured time period.
